decisions.executionNote: Approach the red nut with the left arm and yellow nut with the right, raising and orienting gradually in elbow-up paths; grasp alignment remains to be checked.
Finish vertical approaches and lower open grippers toward the red and yellow nuts, keeping each arm on its own side.
Refine nut centers using the wrist views, close both grippers, and lift to check retention before moving toward matching bolts.
Both nuts appear retained. Move them above the same-color bolts with clearance; compensate the yellow nut's off-center grasp and pause for visual alignment.
Lower toward thread engagement, correcting yellow's lateral offset. Hold closed and inspect bolt visibility inside each nut before tightening.
Begin clockwise tightening with small axial descent. Yellow is held off-center, so orbit its wrist about the inferred nut axis rather than translating the nut during rotation.
Release for a fresh tightening stroke. Reset the left wrist without turning the red nut backward, and recenter the right gripper over the yellow nut for a more symmetric grasp.
Center the yellow nut in its wrist view, close both jaws, and perform a small clockwise threading stroke with gentle axial advance. Verify engagement visually after the stroke.
Reset both wrists with jaws open, maintaining the nuts on their bolts. Make a small visual correction to yellow's eccentric grasp before another tightening stroke.
The yellow nut is now centered in the wrist view. Close both grippers and apply another clockwise tightening stroke, with only slight downward following motion.
Open and reset the wrists for the next clockwise stroke, preserving both nut positions and arm configurations; reclose only after the return rotation.
Continue clockwise tightening of red and yellow while following the thread with millimeter-scale downward motion; keep jaws fully commanded closed during rotation.
Reset open wrists through a larger but continuous rotation for another tightening stroke; leave both nuts seated without reversing their threads.
Apply another clockwise tightening stroke to both aligned pairs, following downward by only 1.6 mm and keeping the grippers commanded closed.
Release and lift away from the red and yellow assemblies. Approach the remaining gray nut with the left hand while the right stays clear in its own workspace.
Lower the left gripper onto the gray nut, refining its center from the calibrated head view. Keep the right arm stationary and clear of the approach.
Correct the gray nut's wrist-view offset, close the left gripper, and lift vertically to test retention before staging it at the center for the right arm.
The gray nut appears retained. Carry it to the shared center staging location and lower it to the table without crossing the arms; the right arm remains clear.
Release the gray nut at center, lift the left hand away, and withdraw it into its own workspace before the right hand approaches the staged nut.
Approach the staged gray nut from the right after the left has cleared center. Begin returning the left arm toward its origin while keeping its elbow-up configuration.
Lower the right gripper to the gray nut's grasp height and pause to inspect centering. Return the left arm to its origin with smooth pose increments.
Refine the right gripper's centering over gray, close it, and lift to verify retention. Settle the left arm at its origin.
Carry the retained gray nut above its matching bolt in the right workspace, keeping clearance and stopping for visual alignment before insertion.
Lower the gray nut onto the aligned gray bolt, keeping its axis vertical and the right gripper closed. Pause at initial engagement before turning.
Begin tightening the engaged gray nut clockwise with gentle axial following. Keep the left hand open at origin and retain wrist-joint margin.
Open and reset the right wrist for the next gray tightening stroke, making a small centering correction while leaving the nut seated on its bolt.
Recenter the gray nut within the open right jaws, regrasp, and make a clockwise tightening stroke with small downward thread following.
The gray bolt is now visible near the nut's top. Release and lift clear to inspect seating, while resetting the right wrist for a safe return toward origin.
All three assemblies appear upright and seated after release. Begin returning the open right hand to origin along a continuous elbow-up path, keeping the left at origin.
Finish returning both open grippers to their starting poses, then settle without disturbing the seated red, yellow, and gray assemblies.
Hold both open hands at origin and allow the three upright matched assemblies to settle; completion is judged from the views rather than tracking residuals.
The red nut's final depth is less clear than the others. Reapproach it with the left hand for a close visual depth check, leaving the gray and yellow pairs undisturbed.
Bring the open left gripper above the red assembly for a close depth check, maintaining clearance and a vertical approach.
The red nut still shows exposed internal threads. Regrasp at its current height and add a gentle clockwise stroke with millimeter-scale axial following.
Finish the red clockwise stroke, release, and start resetting the open wrist. Maintain small axial advancement and avoid disturbing the other assemblies.
Complete the open-wrist reset, regrasp the red nut slightly lower, and begin another controlled clockwise stroke to improve its seating depth.
Finish the red tightening stroke, open the left gripper, and lift clear to inspect the released assembly before returning to origin.
The released red assembly remains upright. Withdraw the left hand with jaws open and reset its wrist at clearance, then return toward origin without disturbing the pairs.
Return the open left hand to its starting pose through a smooth elbow-up motion, keeping the right hand at origin and all three released assemblies untouched.
